_note: SYNTHETIC interviews for the demo. Every person, organization, address, phone number, email and ID below is fictional. Phone numbers use the reserved 555-01xx range and emails use example.com.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: Thanks for joining today. To start, could you tell me a little about yourself and how you usually book medical appointments?

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: Sure. My name is Maria Delgado, I'm a nurse at Riverside Community Hospital, and I live in Ann Arbor with my two kids.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: Honestly, I book almost everything by phone. I call the front desk at 734-555-0142 and just hope someone picks up before my shift starts.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: What happens when nobody picks up?

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: I leave a voicemail and then forget about it. Last month I missed a pediatric checkup for my son Leo because the callback came while I was in surgery prep.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: The portal exists, but it asks for my patient ID, which is MRN 48213977, and I can never find the card.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: If you could change one thing about booking, what would it be?

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: Let me see open slots the way I see my work schedule. Doctor Patel's office sends reminders to maria.delgado@example.com, but only after I've already booked.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: I don't need anything fancy. I just want to book in under a minute from the parking lot, without remembering a password.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: That's really helpful. Thank you, that's everything for today.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: Can you walk me through a typical commute?

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: I'm James Okafor. I take the number 4 bus from Packard Street to the Blake Transit Center, then walk to my job at Northwind Logistics.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: The schedule app says the bus is three minutes away, and then it just disappears. I've been late twice this month, and my manager, Susan Reyes, noticed.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: How do you decide when to leave home?

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: I check the app, then I text my neighbor Priya at 313-555-0187 because she rides the same route and she's more reliable than the app.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: On snowy days I give up and pay for a ride share, which is about fifteen dollars each way. That really adds up.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: What would make you trust the arrival times again?

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: If it told me when it was guessing. Like, this time is live, or this time is just the timetable. Then I could plan around it.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.text: And a way to report a missing bus. I emailed feedback at james.okafor@example.com once and never heard anything back.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: Great. Thanks so much for your time.
